CurrentState.completed-closure-gate: GRACE packet truth now reflects the actual closed state of the repo.
The final ordered closure verification matrix for contracts, runtime, coverage, and docs is published and current.

ExecutionPacket.purpose: Implement one bounded slice of the inbox-first architecture without reintroducing removed public product wording.
ExecutionPacket.contract-excerpt: Use media_item, collection/inbox, selection, analysis_run, source, artifact, diagnostics, retention, and owner scope as the canonical vocabulary.
ExecutionPacket.verification-excerpt: Run the focused checks assigned to the packet and prove stale public product vocabulary did not return.

ArchitecturePacket.purpose: Rewrite GRACE requirements, technology, development, verification, knowledge graph, and operational packet artifacts around the final inbox-first model.
ArchitecturePacket.contract-excerpt: The final product model is media_item -> collection/inbox -> immutable selection -> analysis_run -> artifacts. Canonical vocabulary is media_item, collection/inbox, selection, analysis_run, source, artifact. Jobs, queue tasks, and execution attempts may exist only as internal backend execution details behind analysis_run. Old public product architecture centered on immediate execution requests, grouped submission state, public source grouping, and user-facing mode toggles is deleted rather than wrapped.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: GRACE docs define only the final inbox-first model.
media_item, collection/inbox, immutable selection, analysis_run, lifecycle statuses, owner scope, retention, diagnostics, and evidence gates are specified.
Old batch-oriented and immediate-execution public product wording is removed instead of preserved as target architecture.
Adapter boundaries for Telegram, Web, and MCP stay thin over API-owned state.
Bottom-up sequencing is recorded for later Beads.

verification.command: xmllint --noout docs/requirements.xml docs/technology.xml docs/development-plan.xml docs/verification-plan.xml docs/knowledge-graph.xml docs/operational-packets.xml
Run the focused stale-vocabulary search required by media-36a across the six GRACE XML files.

ExecutionPacket.purpose: Replace public contracts with canonical inbox-first schemas and routes.
ExecutionPacket.contract-excerpt: Define public DTOs and routes for media_item, source, collection, inbox, selection, analysis_run, artifact, diagnostic, owner scope, lifecycle, retention, idempotency, pagination, optimistic version checks, and error envelopes.

implementation-notes.note: Public clients create analysis_run from a sealed selection only.
Contracts must include text, URL, generic file, photo/image, audio/voice, and video/document inputs.
Schema tests must fail if removed public product vocabulary reappears.

verification.check: OpenAPI parses and schema tests pass.
Focused search proves public contracts use canonical vocabulary.

ExecutionPacket.purpose: Implement storage and API orchestration bottom-up before adapter rewrites.
ExecutionPacket.contract-excerpt: Persist sources, media_items, collections, collection_items, immutable selections, analysis_runs, artifacts, diagnostics, retention state, and internal execution rows. Enforce owner scope on every operation.

implementation-notes.note: Create an inbox for each owner and put accepted media_item records there by default.
Seal selection snapshots before scheduling execution.
Use diagnostics for invalid media, invalid selection, unavailable source, worker failure, artifact expiry, retention denial, and adapter conflict.
Keep internal execution rows behind analysis_run and out of the public product contract.

verification.check: Storage tests cover owner isolation, collection versioning, immutable selection, lifecycle, retention, diagnostics, and artifact linkage.
API tests cover media ingestion, inbox, collection mutation, selection creation, analysis_run creation, events, cancellation, artifact access, and diagnostics query.

ExecutionPacket.purpose: Move execution behind analysis_run while consuming only sealed selection snapshots.
ExecutionPacket.contract-excerpt: Workers claim internal execution rows by analysis_run_id, load sealed selection material through internal API contracts, publish artifacts and diagnostics, and never read mutable collection state as execution input.

verification.check: Worker tests prove sealed selection consumption, artifact publication, partial success diagnostics, cancellation phase recording, and no mutation of selections.

ExecutionPacket.purpose: Adapt Telegram to capture media into API-owned inbox and manage selections and runs explicitly.
ExecutionPacket.contract-excerpt: Telegram turns messages, files, URLs, media groups, voice, audio, video, photos, images, and documents into add_media calls. It renders inbox or collection state after accepted input and exposes explicit actions to manage items, create a selection, start analysis_run, view diagnostics, and retrieve artifacts.

verification.check: Telegram tests prove accumulation without user-facing execution modes and prove callbacks use API identifiers plus version checks where mutation is allowed.

ExecutionPacket.purpose: Build Web as the full management surface for inbox-first media analysis.
ExecutionPacket.contract-excerpt: Web manages inbox, collections, media details, selection builder, analysis_run list and detail, artifacts, diagnostics, owner-scoped search, and retention actions over the public API.

verification.check: Web tests prove collection edits after run creation do not alter run selection snapshots.

ExecutionPacket.purpose: Expose MCP tools over the same API-owned media state.
ExecutionPacket.contract-excerpt: MCP tools: add_media, list_media, search_media, get_media, remove_media, get_inbox, create_collection, list_collections, get_collection, update_collection, update_collection_items, create_selection, get_selection, run_analysis, list_runs, get_run, cancel_run, retry_run, list_run_events, list_artifacts, get_artifact, get_artifact_preview, refresh_artifact, and get_diagnostics.

verification.check: MCP tests prove tool behavior matches API owner-scope, lifecycle, retention, and diagnostics envelopes.

RuntimePacket.purpose: Prove the complete inbox-first flow after contracts, server, workers, and adapters converge.

verification.check: Runtime smoke ingests input, lists it in inbox, seals selection, starts analysis_run, observes events, retrieves artifacts, reads diagnostics, denies cross-owner access, and applies retention without corrupting run history.
Focused stale vocabulary search passes across active docs and public contracts.

HotfixPacket.purpose: Fix API-owned inbox ingestion when an owner already has active collection_items.
HotfixPacket.contract-excerpt: New media_item records remain API-owned and append to inbox or named collection membership using the next active collection position. Telegram, Web, and MCP must not carry durable local inbox state or legacy fallback buffers.

verification.check: Focused SQL storage regression proves existing inbox and target collection appends do not reuse position 0.
Storage and API package tests pass.
Compose API accepts a second media_item for an owner with an existing inbox item.

HotfixPacket.purpose: Fix Telegram status refresh failure caused by empty diagnostics lists encoded as null.
HotfixPacket.contract-excerpt: Public paginated list envelopes must encode items as an array on every page, including empty diagnostics, artifacts, media, run, and event pages. Adapters must not need legacy local fallback state to render an empty API-owned result.

verification.check: Focused API regression proves nil source slices encode as items: [] through the shared paging helper.
Live diagnostics endpoint for the Telegram owner returns items: [] for an empty run diagnostic page.
Telegram gateway restore_status completes against the live API for the affected owner and terminal run.

HotfixPacket.purpose: Fix Telegram callback UI refresh when the inbox collection becomes empty after mutation.
HotfixPacket.contract-excerpt: Collection envelopes must expose items as an array even when the collection is empty. Telegram callback UI refresh depends on the API-owned inbox shape and must not require adapter-local fallback rendering for null collection items.

verification.check: Focused storage regression proves GetCollection returns an empty items slice instead of nil.
Focused API regression proves GET /v1/collections/inbox encodes items: [] for an empty inbox collection.
Live restore_status against the affected Telegram owner renders after the empty inbox collection response without callback-handler errors.

HotfixPacket.purpose: Fix Telegram inbox callback UX so the visible surface follows inbox collection membership.
HotfixPacket.contract-excerpt: Telegram inbox pagination, remove, and clear-visible actions must render the API-owned inbox collection membership, not the broader owner media inventory. Refresh actions may no-op safely when Telegram reports the message is not modified.

verification.check: Focused gateway regression proves collection-only removal changes the visible inbox surface even when owner-wide media inventory still contains the removed items.
Focused runtime regression proves refresh tolerates Telegram message-not-modified responses.
Live restore_status for the affected owner shows zero visible inbox items when the inbox collection is empty.

HotfixPacket.purpose: Make Telegram status text and actions Russian-first and easier to understand.
HotfixPacket.contract-excerpt: Telegram status text and button labels must explain refresh, collection mutations, and focused-run files or diagnostics in Russian. Completed historical runs must not appear as generic main-card result actions for a new or unstarted inbox selection.

verification.check: Focused telegram-bot tests prove Russian-first callback copy, status text, and button semantics.
Live restored status text for the affected Telegram owner is Russian-first and renders the current inbox state clearly.

HotfixPacket.purpose: Scope Telegram result and diagnostics buttons to the current analysis_run focus and clear active collection membership after successful result delivery.
HotfixPacket.contract-excerpt: Telegram main-card result and diagnostics buttons are shown only for the analysis_run launched from the current card focus. Successful manual or automatic result delivery clears active inbox or collection membership through the collection mutation API and preserves immutable historical selections, runs, artifacts, and diagnostics.

verification.check: Focused gateway regressions prove historical terminal runs do not create generic result buttons and focused terminal runs produce callbacks for their own analysis_run_id.
Focused runtime regression proves manual result delivery sends the transcript and clears the active collection membership.

HotfixPacket.purpose: Add a Telegram cancel action for the focused active transcription run.
HotfixPacket.contract-excerpt: Telegram shows Отмена only for the current focused queued or running analysis_run. The cancel callback carries the analysis_run id and version, verifies the focused card state, calls the API-owned cancel route, and then refreshes the card without exposing stale cancellation against another run.

verification.check: API client regression proves the Telegram adapter posts to /v1/analysis-runs/{analysis_run_id}/cancel with owner query and cancellation message.
Gateway and runtime regressions prove cancel is shown only for a focused active run, rejects stale focus, calls the API cancel path, and removes the cancel action after refresh.

HotfixPacket.purpose: Make the Telegram transcription launch action visually emphasized and last in the main-card keyboard.
HotfixPacket.contract-excerpt: Telegram main-card keyboards show management actions first and the emphasized 🎙 Транскрибация launch action as the final row, while preserving the existing run callback payload and API-owned collection/version semantics.

verification.check: Focused Telegram keyboard regressions prove Материалы remains first and the accented transcription launch button is the last row.

HotfixPacket.purpose: Hide duplicate Telegram transcription launch while the card is focused on an active transcription run.
HotfixPacket.contract-excerpt: Telegram main-card keyboards must not expose a duplicate transcription launch action while the current card is focused on an active analysis_run. Background active runs are tracked separately and do not block launching a new current selection.

verification.check: Focused Telegram keyboard regressions prove focused active runs remove the transcription launch callback.
Runtime regressions prove background active runs remain cancelable while new material selections can still launch.

HotfixPacket.purpose: Remove the Telegram dead-end state where an active run is visible but neither cancel nor new transcription actions are available.
HotfixPacket.contract-excerpt: Telegram separates background active tasks from the current material selection. If the card is not focused on an active run, the latest visible active run remains cancelable and the current materials can launch a new transcription as an independent analysis_run.

verification.check: Gateway regressions prove unfocused active runs show both cancellation and the emphasized transcription launch action.
Runtime regressions prove an unfocused active run can be canceled and a new transcription can still be launched from the current material selection.

HotfixPacket.purpose: Make public analysis_run cancellation cooperative before terminal worker completion.
HotfixPacket.contract-excerpt: Public cancel requests terminally cancel unclaimed queued analysis_run records, but claimed runs first move to cancel_requested so the worker can observe cancellation and finalize. If worker finalization races with cancel_requested, cancellation wins and the run resolves as canceled.

verification.check: Storage regressions prove unclaimed cancel, claimed cancel_requested, and late worker success resolving as canceled.
API runtime regression proves FinalizeExecution coerces cancel_requested or canceled runs to canceled.
